## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sammutiñāṇakathā* ("Discourse on Conventional Knowledge") is the sixth debate in the fifth chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, situated within the Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. In his doctrinal guide to the Abhidhamma, Nyanatiloka classifies this section as the forty-ninth debate of the *Kathāvatthu*, addressing the proposition of whether conventional knowledge (*sammutiñāṇa*) has only truth, and nothing else, as its object [Nyanatiloka 2007]. According to the traditional Theravāda exegesis, this thesis was advocated by the Andhaka school, who were criticized for failing to distinguish between conventional truth (*sammuti*) and ultimate truth (*paramattha*) [Nyanatiloka 2007]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation in a single language [SuttaCentral].

No cross-language parallels are cataloged on SuttaCentral or detected by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus detects automated text reuse across 130 matching passages with 14 other texts [DharmaNexus]. The highest volume of shared phrasing occurs with neighboring or thematically related *Kathāvatthu* chapters, notably the *Viparītakathā* (Kv 5.3), *Cittārammaṇakathā* (Kv 5.7), *Anantarapaccayakathā* (Kv 14.3), and *Ñāṇakathā* (Kv 20.2), alongside passages shared with the *Paṭṭhāna* (*Mahantaraduka*, Patthana 2.10) and Sutta discourses such as the *Anaṅgaṇa Sutta* (MN 5) [DharmaNexus].
